newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Fiat 1996 oper profits seen lower.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Fiat 1996 oper profits seen lower.

text.p: Italian industrial giant Fiat is expected to report lower 1996 operating profits this week but gains from the partial flotation of its New Holland division should help the pretax and net profit lines, analysts said.
Fiat issues its traditional "letter to shareholders" on Thursday when the company releases its preliminary figures for 1996 which are set to include annual sales, operating profits and cash flow.

Analysts expect Fiat to have continued to be hurt by the depressed state of the Italian domestic car market in 1996, a strong lira and the heavy investment in start-up cost such as its Palio "world car" in south America.

Analysts see Fiat's sales line boosted to around 80 trillion lire from 1995's 75.69 trillion, but operating profits are seen falling to around 2.3-2.8 trillion lire from the 3.305 trillion reported in 1995.

Fiat will report full 1996 figures in a few months' time when the data should show the one-off gain made when it floated 31 percent of agricultural and construction division New Holland on the New York stock market in November 1996 and also capital gains from selling fund management arm Prime to Generali.
Analyst believed that gains from these operations will help 1996 net profits come in above 1995's level of 2.15 trillion lire at around 2.45 trillion lire.

Fiat reported in September its first half 1996 pretax profits slipped 28 percent to 1.547 trillion lire from 2.153 trillion in 1995, and even stripping out extraordinary gains that boosted 1995 results the pre-tax result fell 12.6 percent.
First half 1996 margins fell to 3.7 percent from 5.2 percent and in the first quarter of 1996 fell further to 2.5 percent.
Analysts expect margins to have improved in the fourth quarter helped by the launch of the new Fiat Marea car in September and due to strong Q4 results at New Holland.
They expect Fiat to be cautious on its outcome for 1997, with only limited comments on the effects of the car buying incentive scheme launched this month in Italy.
